articles.title: DukaanDost AI: A Local Gemma Assistant for Stock, Orders, and Udhaar
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle. I built DukaanDost AI, a local business assistant for small Indian distributors supplying biscuits, namkeen, ch…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle . What I Built I built DukaanDost AI , a local business assistant for small Indian distributors supplying biscuits, namkeen, chips, and other packaged goods to shops. Consider a simple transaction: a shop orders several cartons, pays part of the bill, and promises to pay the rest later. The distributor needs to update stock, record the sale, and carry the unpaid amount into the shop’s udhaar , or outstanding balance. DukaanDost brings those tasks together: Inventory tracking with purchases, adjustments, and low-stock alerts. Multi-product orders with cash, UPI, and credit payments. Shop ledgers and partial-payment tracking. Sales reports, estimated gross profit, printable receipts, and CSV export.

articles.title: How we ship a native macOS client for classic MU Online Season 6 (Zenaria x40)
articles.excerpt: MU Online is a Windows-only game from the early 2000s. On a Mac people have usually tried CrossOver (CodeWeavers lists MU as "Installs, Will Not Run") or a Windows VM in Parallels, which tends to lag…
articles.body: MU Online is a Windows-only game from the early 2000s. On a Mac people have usually tried CrossOver (CodeWeavers lists MU as "Installs, Will Not Run") or a Windows VM in Parallels, which tends to lag on Apple Silicon. I run a classic Season 6 server called Zenaria, and we ship a native macOS client for it. Here is how it is put together and what had to be fixed along the way. Disclosure: this is my own project, the server is Zenaria x40. Starting point: not from scratch I did not write a client from zero. There is an open-source project, MuMain: the Season 5.2 client source code that the community has been cleaning up and bringing to Season 6 for years. One of its main changes is that rendering moved to SDL GPU, a layer that talks DirectX 12 on Windows and Metal on macOS.

articles.title: My screenshots were smaller as PNG-8 than JPEG, and my photos were 3.8x bigger
articles.excerpt: For my final-year project I added a small "compress before upload" step, and I gave it exactly one setting: re-encode everything as JPEG at quality 80. Photos came out fine. Screenshots did not. Text…
articles.body: For my final-year project I added a small "compress before upload" step, and I gave it exactly one setting: re-encode everything as JPEG at quality 80. Photos came out fine. Screenshots did not. Text picked up a grey haze around every character, and the files were bigger than I expected for such simple images. So I flipped it and tried saving photos as 256-colour PNG instead, which made them several times larger. One setting, two kinds of image, two different failures. I wanted to understand why before picking a new rule, so I measured four images. The setup was deliberately small. Two screenshots I made myself by rendering made-up pages in a browser and capturing them at 1280×800: a Chinese meeting-notes page with only 174 distinct colours, and an admin order table with 1,402.
articles.author: yue xing

articles.title: My upload pipeline turned every screenshot into JPEG. The text got noisy and the files were bigger than PNG-8
articles.excerpt: My small tool site gets more screenshots than photos. For a long time the upload handler treated them all the same way: decode, re-encode as JPEG, store. Then a user sent me a screenshot of a chat log…
articles.body: My small tool site gets more screenshots than photos. For a long time the upload handler treated them all the same way: decode, re-encode as JPEG, store. Then a user sent me a screenshot of a chat log and asked why the text looked fuzzy after upload. I went back and measured, and the short version is that JPEG was the wrong call for screenshots twice over. The text picked up a ring of noise, and the file was not even smaller than the lossless alternative. Reproducing it without user data I didn't want to test on a user's image, so I made two of my own. I wrote two throwaway pages and captured them at 1280×800. One is a page of Chinese meeting notes with made-up content (174 distinct colors). The other is a fake admin order table (1,402 colors).

articles.body: Apple has finally announced its long-rumored foldable: the iPhone Duo . The new phone has a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display, a “nano‑texture” finish on the inner screen, and barely any visible crease. Instead of Face ID, it uses Touch ID on the power button. It has two cameras, a main lens and a wide-angle lens. Apple completely revamped iOS 27’s controls and apps for the foldable, including putting the dock on the side of the phone. And it has a flashy opening animation when you unfold the phone. The iPhone Duo a big new bet from Apple, though one that’s a little late to the game compared to competitors like Samsung and Google. The phone isn’t cheap: it starts at $1,999 for the base 256GB model, and the prices only go up from there.

articles.excerpt: The astronauts of SpaceX's Crew-12 mission wish that we could all see Earth as they just did —as a beautiful but fragile outpost of life in a vast void.
articles.body: The astronauts of SpaceX's Crew-12 mission to the International Space Station wish that we could all see Earth as they just did. An orbital view reveals the immense beauty of our blue planet, the only world we know of that hosts life. But it also highlights how fragile that life is, tethered to our lonely Earth in the vast void of space, according to Crew-12 commander Jessica Meir of NASA. "You see this very thin, tenuous band of an atmosphere , and you know that that is all that is supporting life, and we really need to do our best to protect it," Meir said on Thursday afternoon (Oct. 15), during a press conference that discussed the recently concluded Crew-12 mission .

articles.title: When not to watch a meteor shower — why I'm not staying up for the Orionids
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week, but a bright moon makes much of the night less than ideal. Sometimes the sensible observing decision is knowing when to stay in bed — and when to get up earl…
articles.body: I used to think being interested in the night sky meant I had to try every meteor shower. If a calendar said "peak," I interpreted that as an instruction. I'd set an alarm, find several layers of clothing and go outside at around 2:00 a.m. when even the neighborhood cats seemed surprised to see me. Then I'd spend an increasingly resentful 45 minutes staring upward, occasionally see one meteor and wonder whether I was somehow doing it all wrong. As I've grown into stargazing, I've become much more selective. The Orionids peak next week, and normally I'd be tempted. These fast meteors come from debris from Halley's Comet , which is enough of a connection to make almost anyone want to go outside.

articles.title: Scientists find 'gemstones' in atmosphere of bizarre, scorching-hot 'marshmallow' exoplanet
articles.excerpt: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers have unravelled some of the secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot exoplanet that has the consistency of marshmallow.
articles.body: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have unraveled some of the atmospheric secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot world that has the consistency of marshmallow. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , under the watchful infrared eye of the JWST , is WASP-17b, located around 1,300 light-years away. The exoplanet has a mass around 0.8 times that of Jupiter, but it is around twice as wide as the solar system's largest planet, giving it a "super-puff" consistency comparable to the Earth-based treat. WASP-17 b is so close to its parent star that it completes an orbit in under four Earth days, with this proximity also making the temperature of this " hot Jupiter " skyrocket.

articles.title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower 2026 peak this week — and when to look
articles.excerpt: The Orionids peak around Oct. 21. Here's when and where to look for the best chance of spotting meteors.
articles.body: If you love watching meteors, 2026 has given you plenty to enjoy. This summer, the annual Perseid meteor shower peaked on the day of a new moon — and a solar eclipse — so moonlight stayed out of the way. And there's more to look forward to: in December, the Geminids, the year's most prolific shower, will peak after a waxing crescent moon sets early in the evening, opening the door to excellent viewing. Right between those two headline showers, the dependable Orionids take their turn, reaching peak activity around Oct. 21-22. So, when and where can you catch the show?
